data.title: Autostart Locations Not Monitored
data.summary:
Persistence was established through user-writable autostart registry keys and startup
folders. The entries survived reboot and logon and produced no alert.
data.description:
Autostart persistence is the first thing an operator reaches for because it needs no
elevation: a standard user can write to their own run keys and startup folder, and the
entry executes at every logon.

It is also one of the easiest things to detect, which is what makes its absence notable.
The locations are few, well known, and change rarely on a managed workstation, so
monitoring them produces a low-volume, high-value signal.

The same properties make them worth baselining. An estate's legitimate autostart entries
are largely uniform, and deviation from that baseline is a strong indicator.
data.recommendation:
* Monitor autostart registry locations and startup folders, and alert on new entries that
  do not match the deployment baseline.
* Baseline the legitimate entries per build so deviation is meaningful.
* Hunt for entries referencing user-writable paths, which have almost no legitimate use.
data.short_recommendation: Baseline autostart locations per build and alert on deviation.

attack_techniques.technique: T1547.001 — Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
